metadata.title: Kendre Miller - Handles eight carries in Paris loss
metadata.description: Miller rushed eight times for six yards in Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers in Paris.
metadata.analysis: The Saints got absolutely nothing going on the ground against Pittsburgh, rushing 17 times for 18 yards as a team, so it's not like Miller and his team-leading eight carries was the only issue. New Orleans heads into its bye in Week 8, and Travis Etienne (hamstring) will be eligible to come off injured reserve for Week 9 against the Browns. When both Etienne and Alvin Kamara were healthy and active together earlier this season, Miller was a healthy inactive.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller held in check on Sunday
metadata.description: Kendre Miller ran eight times for six yards and caught three of five targets for 22 yards in the Saints' 16-10 loss to the Steelers.
metadata.analysis: Miller went from having 20 carries last week for 70 yards to averaging less than one yard per carry. He's a very inconsistent asset; Travis Etienne Jr. will be back soon, and Alvin Kamara is still acting as the primary receiving back. Miller is not someone you can confidently start.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller a Priority Week 7 Waiver Add as Backfield Role Expands
metadata.description: New Orleans Saints running back Kendre Miller is a priority waiver add as his share of the backfield grows during Travis Etienne Jr.'s (hamstring) absence, and the increased workload makes him a viable RB2 or flex option against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 7, particularly for managers seeking immediate help in 10-team and deeper leagues. His offensive snap rate increased from 31% in Week 5 to 44% against the New York Giants, when he handled 20 of New Orleans' 33 running back carries. Miller rushed for 70 yards, while Alvin Kamara managed seven attempts and CJ Donaldson had six. Kamara (back) was limited throughout the practice week but carries no injury designation, and he remains involved in the passing game after recording 35 receiving yards and a touchdown against the Giants. Miller's receiving contribution has been minimal, with two catches for zero yards in Week 6. Etienne could return after the Saints' Week 8 bye, which potentially limits Miller's longer-term value.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller Looks to Build on Solid Week 6 Performance
metadata.description: New Orleans Saints running back Kendre Miller rushed 20 times for 70 yards in Week 6's win over the Giants. Miller easily outpaced his fellow backs in touches, with 22 compared to nine for Alvin Kamara and six for C.J. Donaldson. The Saints' offensive line was finally able to create some running lanes for Miller, who took advantage with a season-high 70 rushing yards. He remains fairly inefficient with the ball, however, averaging just 3.5 yards per carry in Week 6 and a career-low 3.1 yards per carry on the season. With Travis Etienne Jr. out for at least one more game, Miller should continue to see a split workload, with Kamara remaining involved. He comes in as RB29 in RotoBaller's rankings this week against a Steelers defense that ranks 13th against the run.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller Seeing Enough Work to Make Him a Plug-and-Play Option
metadata.description: In a Week 6 win over the Giants, New Orleans Saints running back Kendre Miller led the team with 70 rushing yards on a career-high 20 carries. With Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) slated to miss at least one more game with the hamstring injury that landed him on Injured Reserve, Miller has waiver appeal as a desperation flex play for Week 7. The Saints' matchup against the Steelers is not ideal, but with four NFL teams on bye and Miller coming off a game in which he handled over a 60% running back rush share and four red zone carries, he boasts enough of a fantasy-friendly role to make him RotoBaller's RB27 heading into the week.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller sees 20 carries Sunday
metadata.description: Kendre Miller ran for 70 yards on 20 carries in the Saints 34-27 win over the Giants.
metadata.analysis: Miller also caught both of his targets for zero yards receiving. He was once again the workhorse on the ground. He'll be a touchdown dependent RB2 next week against the Steelers.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller - Leading rusher in Week 6 win
metadata.description: Miller carried the ball 20 times for 70 yards and caught both his targets for zero yards in Sunday's 34-27 win over the Giants.
metadata.analysis: Alvin Kamara missed time in the first half due to an undisclosed injury, and while he was able to return and make an impact as a pass catcher, Miller led the Saints in rushing yards and touches with 22. The 70 yards also represented his best total since Week 18 of his rookie season in 2023. With Travis Etienne (hamstring) not eligible to return until after a Week 8 bye, Miller should split reps in the backfield with Kamara once again in Week 7 against the Steelers in Paris.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller Could See Another Opportunity to Lead Saints Backfield
metadata.description: New Orleans Saints running back Kendre Miller handled the bulk of the carries in Week 5 against the Vikings, recording 10 rushes for 30 yards and a touchdown. With starting running back Alvin Kamara entering the game after a week of limited practices due to a back issue, Miller played just 31% of the snaps but handled 71% of the team's carries. With Kamara listed as questionable with a back injury again this week, Miller could continue to lead the Saints' backfield. His efficiency remains a concern, as he is averaging just 3.9 yards per carry, and he has seen little involvement in the passing game, recording only four receptions for 15 yards this season. If Kamara is unable to suit up, Miller is worth considering as a low-end RB2/FLEX option against a Giants defense allowing 127.6 rushing yards per game.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller - Finds end zone in Week 5 loss
metadata.description: Miller turned 10 carries into 30 yards and a touchdown during the Saints' 23-13 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Miller averaged only 3.0 YPC during Sunday's loss, but his two-yard touchdown run midway through the second quarter gave the Saints an early 7-3 lead, although New Orleans' offense generated only three more points the rest of the way. His 10 carries led the Saints' backfield that also includes CJ Donaldson (four carries) and Alvin Kamara (three), though Miller had only three rushes during the second half. Kamara dealt with a back issue during Week 5 prep, and if that issue continues to linger, then Miller could be the Saints' lead back for Week 6 against the Giants this Sunday.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller a Viable Deep-League Streamer Option
metadata.description: New Orleans Saints running back Kendre Miller has seen a ton of usage in his team's offense to this point in 2026, recording 29 carries for 83 yards and two touchdowns across four games. However, the 24-year-old may be emerging as the leader of the Saints backfield in the short term. Saints RB1 Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) is currently on Injured Reserve and is not eligible to return until Week 9. While veteran back Alvin Kamara is the most established healthy name in the New Orleans running back room, Miller led the team in touches in Week 5. Kamara has also been extremely inefficient as a rusher over the last two seasons, averaging just 3.5 yards per carry since the start of 2025. Heading into a favorable Week 6 matchup against the New York Giants, Miller could be a potential deep-league streamer for fantasy managers to target on the waiver wire.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller reaches end zone in Week 5 loss to Vikings
metadata.description: Kendre Miller carried the ball 10 times for 30 yards and one touchdown in the Saints' 23-13 Week 5 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
metadata.analysis: Miller has made minimal impact out of the New Orleans backfield to this point, rushing for less than 40 yards in each of his four contests. The running back remains difficult to trust in all formats ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the New York Giants.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller Could See Increased Role Against the Vikings
metadata.description: New Orleans Saints running back Kendre Miller rushed six times for nine yards and added two receptions for 10 yards in Week 4's loss to the Falcons. The TCU product has been very inefficient with the ball, averaging just 2.8 yards per carry and 3.75 yards per reception while also recording one lost fumble and only one touchdown. It was thought that Miller could have some standalone value with fellow running back Travis Etienne Jr. on IR, but he simply has not done enough with his touches to warrant much excitement from fantasy managers. Despite this, he should still be rostered as a handcuff for now, as starter Alvin Kamara is questionable for Week 5 with a back issue. If Kamara is unable to suit up, Miller would step into the RB1 role, but faces a difficult matchup against a Vikings defense allowing the fewest PPR points to running backs. He is ranked as RB43 in RotoBaller's rankings this week.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller Could be a Flex Option if Teammate Misses Time
metadata.description: New Orleans Saints running back Kendre Miller had six carries for nine yards and two receptions for 10 yards in the 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons. With starting running back Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) on injured reserve, both Miller and veteran Alvin Kamara saw an increased workload despite trailing for most of the game. Kamara played 38% of the snaps, while Miller played just 26%, with rookie CJ Donaldson handling two-minute situations. The backfield looked ugly for fantasy managers in Week 4, but Kamara limped off the field to the medical tent with what appeared to be a knee injury. While he later returned to the game, Kamara has had multiple knee sprains throughout his career, including one during training camp that cost him the first week of the season. Fantasy managers should track whether Kamara misses practice time throughout the week, as Miller would become a FLEX option in Week 5.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller - Six carries in defeat
metadata.description: Miller rushed six time for nine yards and caught two of three targets while losing a fumble in Monday night's 45-24 loss to Atlanta.
metadata.analysis: Miller was rumored to be on track for a larger workload in Week 4 after starting running back Travis Etienne (hamstring) was placed on injured reserve. Miller was only on the field for 26 percent of the team's offensive snaps, which could have been as a result of a first-quarter fumble that Atlanta ultimately recovered. Veteran Alvin Kamara was on the field for 41 percent of the offensive snaps, turning seven carries into 23 yards and two scores while also reeling in five of seven targets for 35 yards in the contest. It appears as if Miller will operate as the No. 2 option behind Kamara in Etienne's absence, making him a low-upside fantasy option.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller struggles in loss Monday
metadata.description: Kendre Miller rushed the ball six times for just nine yards and lost a fumble in Monday night's 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons.
metadata.analysis: Miller had a bad game on Monday night. He totaled just 19 yards on the ground and through the air against the Falcons, and he also lost a costly fumble, which further hurt his fantasy total. He should not be started in any fantasy league formats moving forward, especially with Alvin Kamara still seeing the bulk of the work in New Orleans' backfield right now.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller Highly Underwhelming with Poor Efficiency Numbers in Week 4
metadata.description: New Orleans Saints running back Kendre Miller rushed for just nine yards on six carries during Monday's Week 4 loss against the Atlanta Falcons. He also caught two of three targets for 10 receiving yards. Outside of the moderate pass-catching role, Miller had a very frustrating performance. Many managers scrambled to add him off waivers after the team placed Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) on injured reserve, thinking that the 24-year-old could lead the backfield or at least have a sizable role alongside Alvin Kamara. For what it's worth, he had just one fewer carry than Kamara, but the veteran back had two touchdowns and also accrued seven targets. Rookie CJ Donaldson also carved out a role, logging 18 rushing yards on three carries. Miller's inefficiency, lack of touchdown volume, and uninspiring receiving contributions will keep him out of the top-36 running back conversation for Week 5 against the Minnesota Vikings.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller Set for Increased Workload in Week 4
metadata.description: New Orleans Saints running back Kendre Miller rushed four times for 14 yards and added two receptions for five yards in Week 3's loss to the Raiders. He was inactive in Week 2, but when called upon in Week 1, Miller looked solid, rushing nine times for 30 yards and a touchdown against the Lions. With a career average of 3.9 yards per attempt, Miller figures to be in line for additional work with starting running back Travis Etienne Jr. out for Week 4. He will likely be part of a timeshare with fellow running back Alvin Kamara and faces a difficult matchup against the Falcons, who surrender a league-low 47.7 rushing yards per game. Miller ranks as RB37 in RotoBaller's rankings for Week 4.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller - In mix for more snaps
metadata.description: Miller is in line for a larger offensive role for as long as Travis Etienne (hamstring) is on injured reserve, John DeShazler of the Saints' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Etienne's placement on IR on Thursday comes after the star running back aggravated a hamstring injury during the Saints' Week 3 loss to the Raiders. With Etienne sidelined, Miller and Alvin Kamara figure to operate as the Saints' top running backs moving forward, with undrafted rookie CJ Donaldson also in the mix for backfield work. Miller has 13 carries for 44 yards (3.4 YPC) and a touchdown along with two catches (on three targets) for five yards through two regular-season games.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller Back in the Waiver Mix for Week 4
metadata.description: New Orleans Saints running back Kendre Miller is back in the waiver mix after Travis Etienne Jr. left Sunday's loss to Las Vegas with a hamstring injury. Miller had four carries for 14 yards and caught two passes for five yards, his first offensive work since Week 1 after sitting out Week 2 as a healthy inactive. There was not much production here, but the path to more work is easy to see if Etienne misses time. Miller handled nine carries for 30 yards and a touchdown in the opener while Alvin Kamara was sidelined, and Kamara is now back to share the backfield. RotoBaller has Miller 24th overall in its Week 4 waiver rankings and recommends him in 12-team leagues. He is not an immediate starter, but managers looking for running back depth can stash him while waiting for more clarity on Etienne's hamstring.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller sees four carries Sunday
metadata.description: Kendre Miller ran for 14 yards on four carries in the Saints 35-27 loss against the Raiders on Sunday. He also caught 2-of-3 targets for five yards receiving.
metadata.analysis: Miller saw some opportunity with Travis Etienne Jr. exiting early. Alvin Kamara was still the lead back in that span.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller - Avoids injury designation for Week 3
metadata.description: Miller (illness) doesn't carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders.
metadata.analysis: Miller was under the weather Thursday, keeping him off the practice field. However, he was a full participant Friday. Miller was a healthy scratch for the 24-17 win over Baltimore in Week 2, meaning he is in danger of suffering the same fate versus Las Vegas, though his services may be needed on special teams with Barion Brown (hamstring) ruled out. With that in mind, if Miller is inactive, that would likely mean more work for Alvin Kamara and CJ Donaldson behind Travis Etienne.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller (illness) returns to practice Friday
metadata.description: Kendre Miller was back at practice on Friday.
metadata.analysis: Miller had been absent due to an illness. He'll need to be monitored when the injury report is released.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller - Sits out practice with illness
metadata.description: Miller was a non-participant in Thursday's practice due to an illness, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
metadata.analysis: After being a healthy inactive Week 2 win over the Ravens while the Saints welcomed Alvin Kamara (knee) back from a one-game absence, Miller will now have to overcome an illness as he looks to re-enter the backfield mix Sunday versus the Raiders. Even if he makes a full recovery from the ailment, Miller may need No. 1 back Travis Etienne (hamstring) to sit out the Week 3 game in order to avoid another inactive status. Etienne has been limited in both of the Saints' practices this week, clouding his availability for Sunday.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller (illness) downgraded to non-participant Thursday
metadata.description: Kendre Miller (illness) was downgraded to a non-participant at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Miller is a new addition to New Orleans' injury report. He's dealing with some kind of an illness right now and wasn't able to practice on Thursday as a result. He's likely day-to-day for the time being, but of he's cleared to play on Sunday and Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) isn't, he will be primed for more work than usual against the Raiders.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller - Healthy scratch in Week 2
metadata.description: Miller (coach's decision) is listed as inactive Sunday in Baltimore.
metadata.analysis: Miller served as the No. 2 RB behind Travis Etienne in Week 1 with Alvin Kamara inactive due to a knee issue, but with Kamara back in action Sunday, Miller will be a healthy scratch. That leaves CJ Donaldson as the active third backfield option behind Etienne and Kamara in Week 2. Miller's next chance for game action is next Sunday against the Raiders.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller officially inactive for Week 2
metadata.description: Saints RB Kendre Miller is officially inactive for the Saints' Week 2 matchup with Baltimore.
metadata.analysis: Miller was not listed on the injury report this week and is a healthy inactive. Alvin Kamara (knee) makes his return to the lineup for the Saints.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller a Healthy Scratch With RB Returning for Saints
metadata.description: New Orleans Saints running back Kendre Miller is a healthy inactive for the Week 2 game on the road against the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday, according to Matthew Paras of The New Orleans Times-Picayune. Miller actually saw nine carries for 30 yards and a touchdown in last week's season-opening overtime loss to the Detroit Lions alongside Travis Etienne Jr. in the Saints' backfield. However, with veteran Alvin Kamara returning from a knee injury that sidelined him in Week 1, the 24-year-old Miller falls back down the depth chart and will not play this weekend. Miller played only 32.2% of the offensive snaps in Detroit last weekend and will remain stuck as the Saints' RB3 going forward as long as both Etienne and Kamara stay healthy.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller's Value in Week 2 Hurt by Returning RB
metadata.description: New Orleans Saints running back Kendre Miller will be extremely hard to trust in Week 2 against the Baltimore Ravens, even though he scored a touchdown against the Detroit Lions in the Week 1 season-opening loss. Miller is the backup running back to Travis Etienne Jr. but is now also behind Alvin Kamara, who is set to return in Week 2. Miller rushed nine times for 30 yards and a score in Week 1. While Miller is a very reliable real-life backup running back, his fantasy value is not off the charts, and he makes for a bit of a risky play against a good Baltimore Ravens defense, especially with the return of Kamara. But in deep leagues, it might be worth taking a chance on more involvement for Miller in the rushing attack and banking on the touchdown upside of the big back. At 6-foot-0 and 220 pounds, Miller has the size necessary to vulture a touchdown away from Etienne, and now Kamara.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller - Finds end zone in Week 1 loss
metadata.description: Miller turned nine carries into 30 yards and a touchdown while adding a 19-yard kickoff return during the Saints' 31-30 overtime loss to the Lions on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: The Saints were kept off the board in the first half, but Miller helped get New Orleans on the board in the third quarter with an eight-yard touchdown run. In the absence of Alvin Kamara (knee), Miller played 29 of 90 offensive snaps (32.2 percent) and operated as the Saints' RB2 behind Travis Etienne (53 offensive snaps). Miller's role on offense would decrease drastically if Kamara was cleared to play against the Ravens in Week 2.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller reaches end zone in Week 1 loss
metadata.description: Kendre Miller carried the ball nine times for 30 yards and one touchdown in the Saints' 31-30 Week 1 loss to the Detroit Lions.
metadata.analysis: Miller saw steady involvement as part of an underperforming New Orleans ground attack, tying for the team lead in carries on an otherwise forgettable day. The running back remains difficult to trust as part of a crowded New Orleans backfield once Alvin Kamara returns, with a Week 2 contest against the Baltimore Ravens up next.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller a Speculative Waiver-Wire Add After Surprising Usage
metadata.description: New Orleans Saints running back Kendre Miller rushed for 30 yards on nine rushing attempts and a touchdown in Sunday's 31-30 loss to the Detroit Lions. Miller logged the Saints' first touchdown with an eight-yard score to cut the lead to 21-7. Surprisingly, the 24-year-old was heavily used in the running back rotation and even vultured starter Travis Etienne Jr.'s touchdown. Miller and Etienne both had nine rushing attempts on Sunday. Etienne was more efficient on the ground, averaging 5.1 yards per carry compared to Miller's 3.3. Still, Miller's usage is puzzling since the Saints signed Etienne to a four-year, $52 million contract this offseason. Miller wasn't targeted, but did log 26 snaps and six routes run in the Week 1 loss. Fantasy managers searching for help at running back can look to add Miller as he's widely available and only rostered in 1% of Fantasy Yahoo leagues. He's a desperation FLEX at best in a road matchup against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 2.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller - Back to practice
metadata.description: Miller was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Miller was dealing with an unknown issue, but the running back's uninhibited presence in practice should cleanse all doubts. The 24-year-old is set to be the No. 2 option behind Travis Etienne for the Saints' Week 1 matchup with the Lions.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller good to go for Week 1
metadata.description: Kendre Miller will be good to go for Week 1's matchup against the Detroit Lions.
metadata.analysis: Miller is going to be good to go for the season opener on Sunday. His status was in question at one point due to some recent injuries that he's been dealing with, but he is over them now and will be fully good to go against the Lions. He will be primed for more work than usual if Alvin Kamara (knee) and Audric Estime (thigh) are both ruled out for this matchup.

metadata.title: Kendre Miller not seen at practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Kendre Miller was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Miller departed practice early on Tuesday. There will be an update on his injury status when available.
